A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
The facility has been observed to have three repeat priority/priority foundation violations from the previous inspection. Person-in-charge is a current Certified Food Protection Manager (21556549). Operator was able to answer questions adequately. Although violations were corrected on-site, all three violations are repeat violations from the previous inspection. Per 2017 FDA Food Code, the person-in-charge must be able to prevent the occurrence of priority/priority foundation violations through active managerial control of the facility. The establishment has not been able to adequately prevent such violations from occurring. As such, a follow-up is issued for 30-days to ensure continued compliance with food separation and protection, cleanliness of food contact surfaces and date-marking. Ensure that these items remain corrected throughout all operations. This is a repeat violation from routine inspection dated 10/27/2022. Inspector will follow-up with facility on Wednesday 12/28/2022. 

2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Inspector observed black, slimy mold growth on the baffle of the ice machine. During the previous routine inspection, the facility was instructed to discard all contaminated ice and clean the ice machine. This was completed satisfactorily by the follow-up on 11/07/2022. During the inspection today, mold growth is observed due to an insufficient cleaning frequency. Water drips from the center of the baffle regularly. This dripping water is observed to be coming from the molded section of the baffle. As such, all ice in the machine must be considered potentially contaminated by the mold on the baffle. The ice was immediately discarded. Corrected on site. Ensure that food (ice) is protected from all sources of contamination during storage. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
The baffle of the ice machine is observed to be soiled with slimy black mold. The baffle of the ice machine is in contact with food and also allows dripping water to land on the ice below. As such, this surface must be cleaned at a frequency that precludes the accumulation of mold and other residue which has the potential to contaminate the ice below. The facility has not maintained a cleaning frequency which is sufficient to ensure compliance with this requirement. Ensure that the baffle and areas behind the baffle of the ice machine are cleaned daily to prevent recurrence of mold growth. This is a repeat violation from previous routine inspection dated 10/27/2022. The baffle has been cleaned with sanitizer; corrected on site. 

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Inspector observed cut celery in the upright cooler across from the ice machine which did not have date marking. Once foods are prepared (cut) dates must be applied and foods must be discarded within 7-days. Discussed proper date marking procedures with person-in-charge who understands that this is a requirement. Ensure that all items prepared and needing to be refrigerated are date marked with the date opened/prepared and/or the date to be discarded. This is a repeat violation from previous inspection dated 10/27/2022. Dates were applied to the cut celery during the inspection; corrected on-site. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
Person-in-charge was personable but lacked understanding of 2017 FDA Food Code requirements including but not limited to paperwork, cleaning procedures, hand washing practices, and date marking. Facility has repeat violations and priority/priority foundation violations. PIC needs to focus on ensuring compliance through active managerial control in the facility and asking questions as appropriate. A 30-day follow-up is being issued to ensure compliance and provide education as necessary to ensure compliance with code moving forward.

The PERSON IN CHARGE shall: (A) FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations not conducted in private home/room with sleeping quarters;  (B) restricted access ; (C) visitors comply with Code; (D) monitor EMPLOYEES' handwashing; (E) monitor deliveries;  (F) approved source/unadulterated;  (G) proper cooking TCS Food; (H) proper cooling ; (I) monitoring temperatures; (J) consumer advisory conveyed; (K) proper sanitizing;  (L) buffets are controlled;  (M) preventing cross-contamination of RTE FOOD with bare hands; (N) EMPLOYEES are properly trained in FOOD; (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of responsibility to report information about health; (P) Written procedures and plans are maintained and implemented as required. Pf

Operator was unaware of this requirement despite being a repeat violation from inspection dated 11/18/2021. Facility was provided with employee health reporting forms during prior inspection which were completed and signed during the inspection. These forms are not available upon request and new forms have not been completed. All employees must have signed employee health reporting agreements with the facility at all times. Ensure that all current and future employees are made aware of this requirement and sign the appropriate acknowledgement. Facility has been provided with another copy of the form and all employees have signed the agreement. Corrected on site. 

2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Inspector observed employees washing their hands and turning the faucet off without using a barrier. Discussed this violation with person in charge who has actively corrected the behavior. Corrected on site. This is a repeat violation from 11/18/2021. Ensure that correct hand washing procedure is followed at ALL TIMES. 

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Inspector observed that ice in the ice machine had water contaminated from molded portions of the ice machine. The area around the outlet for the ice was heavily soiled with thick black mold and residue. In the stored ice, inspector observed small black particles and a relatively large piece of slimy molded material which had fallen from the above areas of the ice machine. Service of ice-based products including soda and other drinks was immediately halted and both the ice machine and soda machine were emptied of ice to facilitate cleaning. 

Upon further inspection of the ice machine, areas of the machine including around the outlet port are heavily molded into areas which are unreachable for cleaning. Molded areas are heavily molded due to the extensive use of abrasive materials to clean the ice machine in the past. These ares of the ice machine are not smooth or easily cleanable. Food contact surfaces must be durable, smooth and easily cleanable. Repair or replace the ice machine to ensure that the interior compartment is smooth and easily cleanable. Ensure that cleaning is performed to remove all mold from the machine. If mold cannot be removed, replacement is necessary. Facility is obtaining ice from a gas station which will be stored in the freezer in the meantime. Inspector will follow-up in 10-days to ensure repair/replacement and cleaning have been completed. Ice from this machine may not be served until inspector has verified compliance.  

Ensure that ice is protected from contamination at ALL times through frequent cleaning and monitoring of containers and equipment. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Ice machine equipment was heavily soiled with mold and other residue. The baffle, sides and ice outlet had a significant buildup of residue the presented a contamination hazard for the ice inside the machine. Ice is a food. Any pieces of the equipment which touch ice must be cleaned regularly to prevent the accumulation of debris and residues. Ice machine was cleaned appropriately during the inspection and no additional mold is observed at this time. Continue ensuring that all food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency that effectively precludes buildup from occurring.

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
Inspector observed PIC leave a wet wiping cloth on the counter top next to the slicer. Person-in-charge stated that the cloth was used for sanitizing the slicing equipment. Wet wiping cloths, when not directly in use for wiping, must be stored in sanitizer solution to prevent contamination. Ensure that wiping cloths are stored in sanitizer when not in use. PIC tossed the cloth and got a new one during the inspection. Corrected on site. 

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

The ice scoop was removed and cleaned. Corrected on site. This is a repeat violation from previous inspection dated 11/18/2021. 

3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.citation_text:
2-501.11 Written procedure with specific actions to be taken in case of a vomit and/or diarrhea incident was not available. Norovirus disinfection handout was provided. Bleach is available for use. Maintain the norovirus disinfection policy on-site along with all other employee health documentation.
A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Food employees were observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off without a barrier. Proper technique poster is available for reference at the front handsink. Handwashing was discussed with store manager. Ensure staff are using proper technique during handwashing process. 
To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink. Use the paper towels after hands are dried and shut off the faucet at the last step of the handwashing process.
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.citation_text:
6-202.15 A hole was present at the bottom right corner of weather stripping on the back door. Provide repairs to seal the hole.
Outer openings of a food establishment shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by providing solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.citation_text:
3-305.11 Bag of onions was observed on the floor in the dry storage area. Store food up off the floor at least 6 inches. 
Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food in a clean, dry location; where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and at least 6 inches above the floor.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.12 Ice scoop was observed on top of the ice machine. Proper storage in a clean, protected location was discussed. 
During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food preparation and dispensing utensils shall be stored in a clean, protected location if the utensils, such as ice scoops, are used only with a food that is not TCS food.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.citation_text:
4-202.11 White baffle in the ice machine was cracked and broken along the lower edge. The baffle needs to be replaced. Manager stated they have spoke with supervisor about getting the baffle replaced. This was a repeat violation during the 2019 routine inspection. Provide a plan of action within 10 days. 
Food-contact surfaces shall be smooth; free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, inclusions, pits, and similar imperfections; and free of sharp internal angles, corners, and crevices.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.citation_text:
4-202.16 Rust was observed on shelving in the three door cooler where coating has begun to wear off. Re-surface the shelving. 
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 & 6-501.12 Floor tile by the wall on the left side of the 3 part sink was loose. General buildup and mold were observed on the underside of the tile and on the floor where tile was loose. Until repairs are done, manager was advised to keep the area clean and dry to eliminate potential food and water sources for pests. Approximately a half dozen fruit flies were observed under the 3 part sink adjacent to the floor tile of concern.  
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair, and cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 Proof of current food handler certification was not available for delivery drivers, and one of the employees that mainly does deliveries was assisting with bread prep. All employees that do not have a food manager certification need to complete the online food handler certification, especially since delivery drivers assist with prep and may also assist with ware washing. Copies of certifications need to be maintained on-site.
All food handlers, other than someone who has a food manager certification, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.
